name: virtio-media host device ABI (guest-side contract for the primary VideoToolbox-backed device)

authority.uapiHeaders: linux-source-6.12_6.12.107-1 (include/uapi), sizes/offsets probed for ARM64 LP64

endianness: All virtio-media protocol structures are little-endian on the wire. V4L2 ioctl payloads are the plain 64-bit (LP64) layout of the corresponding struct v4l2_* as defined by the 6.12 UAPI headers; guest is aarch64 LP64, host must marshal to/from this exact layout (the primary's emulator marshals between this layout and its internal representation).

virtqueues.name: commandq
virtqueues.driverToDevice: all commands; device MUST return used descriptor chains promptly and never hold them indefinitely

virtqueues.name: eventq
virtqueues.deviceToDriver: all events; driver re-queues returned descriptor chains promptly (16 pre-queued event buffers of VIRTIO_MEDIA_EVENT_MAX_SIZE=608 bytes each)

featureBits.VIRTIO_F_ACCESS_ORDER: optional, driver does not rely on it
featureBits.sharedMemoryRegions: device MUST expose SHM region id VIRTIO_MEDIA_SHM_MMAP(0) for MMAP buffers; if absent, V4L2_MEMORY_MMAP is unusable and only USERPTR works

layout.meaning: copied verbatim to v4l2_capability.capabilities AND device_caps by the guest driver; VFL_DIR is derived from it (M2M caps => VFL_DIR_M2M)
enum vfl_devnode_type; use 0 (VFL_TYPE_VIDEO) so the node registers as /dev/videoX
UTF-8 card name; the guest driver hardcodes driver name 'virtio-media' (vd->name), card comes from QUERYCAP via ioctl not from config

semantics: Guest driver issues VIRTIO_MEDIA_CMD_MMAP with offset=<v4l2_buffer.m.offset from VIDIOC_QUERYBUF/VIDIOC_QBUF>; device answers driver_addr (u64 offset into region 0) and len.

Guest maps [region0.base + driver_addr, +len) into the process address space. vm_pgoff presented to userspace becomes (driver_addr + region0.base)>>PAGE_SHIFT; userspace mmap()s /dev/videoX with that pgoff.
Mapping size must be <= PAGE_ALIGN(len); VM_SHARED and VM_READ|VM_WRITE are required (driver rejects otherwise).

MUNMAP (driver vma close) sends VIRTIO_MEDIA_CMD_MUNMAP with driver_addr; device must refcount: repeated MMAP of the same buffer offset must return the same driver_addr, and storage must persist until munmap (and until the device finishes all in-flight reads/writes of the buffer).

Region size is fixed at device creation (device decision); all buffer offsets must stay within it. Zero-copy: compressed bitstream MMAP buffers for OUTPUT queues and raw frame MMAP buffers for CAPTURE queues both live here.

commands.note: All command/response structs below are the exact vendored layout; sizes/offsets verified by scripts/abi_probe.c on ARM64 LP64 (output: scripts/abi_probe_out.jsonl).

VIRTIO_MEDIA_CMD_OPEN.semantics: One per opened /dev/videoX file. session_id is scoped to this virtio device. Device may limit concurrent sessions; return -EMFILE/-ENOSPC style errors to refuse.

VIRTIO_MEDIA_CMD_CLOSE.resp: none (fire-and-forget); device releases all session state: queued buffers, mappings, subscribed events
VIRTIO_MEDIA_CMD_CLOSE.semantics: Sent on last file close. After this the session_id must not be reused by either side.

VIRTIO_MEDIA_CMD_IOCTL.payloadRule: code = _IOC_NR only. Payload size = the full 64-bit UAPI struct size (NOT _IOC_SIZE, which is capped at 16383 and equal for our structs anyway). Direction from _IOC_DIR: _IOR => payload in device-writable section after resp; _IOW => payload after cmd in device-readable section; _IOWR => payload in BOTH sections (device reads cmd copy, writes resp copy).

VIRTIO_MEDIA_CMD_MUNMAP.semantics: driver_addr must equal a value previously returned by CMD_MMAP; device drops its refcount on that mapping.

VIRTIO_MEDIA_EVT_ERROR.semantics: Unrecoverable session error; guest driver considers the session corrupted and closes it. errno = Linux error code.

fields.planes: 96:512 reserved (single-planar v4l2_buffer carries no plane array; zeros)

VIRTIO_MEDIA_EVT_DQBUF.semantics: Device->driver notification that a single-planar v4l2_buffer completed. Sent for both OUTPUT (compressed-in) and CAPTURE (raw-out) queues.

VIRTIO_MEDIA_EVT_EVENT.semantics: V4L2 event delivery for subscribed events (e.g. V4L2_EVENT_EOS, V4L2_EVENT_SOURCE_CHANGE, decoder resolution-change).

events.ordering: Events for a session are delivered in order on eventq. DQBUF for a given buffer is delivered exactly once. After VIRTIO_MEDIA_EVT_ERROR no further events carry that session_id.

bufferIoctlWireLayout.note: Applies to VIDIOC_QBUF(15), VIDIOC_DQBUF(17), VIDIOC_QUERYBUF(16), VIDIOC_PREPARE_BUF(93). These use the dedicated scatterlist_builder_add_buffer path, NOT the plain payload rule.

deviceReadable: struct v4l2_buffer (88) — single-planar; .length is the mapped byte length
no plane array follows: the compiled host device rejects multi-planar M2M buffer types
if memory==V4L2_MEMORY_USERPTR: virtio_media_sg_entry[.] describing user payload pages
deviceWritable: no plane array: single-planar v4l2_buffer only
QBUF_QUERYBUF_DQBUF.semantics: For MMAP memory the payload bytes themselves are NOT in the descriptor chain — the device reads/writes them through SHM region 0 at v4l2_buffer.m.offset. MMAP QBUF exchanges only the single-planar v4l2_buffer metadata. USERPTR is not implemented by the host device.

requiredIoctlSet.comment: Finite set the primary must implement for stock FFmpeg/v4l2-ctl stateful M2M. All are pure pass-through semantics: the device plays the role of an in-kernel V4L2 driver. Full v4l2_ioctl_ops table is forwarded by the guest driver; unsupported ioctls should return -ENOTTY/-EINVAL just like a real driver.

identity.must: driver='virtio-media', card=config card, capabilities|device_caps from config, device_caps=V4L2_CAP_VIDEO_M2M|V4L2_CAP_STREAMING

buffers.note: must return buffer m.offset values that are stable per (session,queue,index) and valid for VIRTIO_MEDIA_CMD_MMAP

streaming.note: device returns the completed buffer synchronously in the response if one is already done; otherwise the ioctl may complete a pending buffer via VIRTIO_MEDIA_EVT_DQBUF per guest driver logic (check driver: vidioc_dqbuf waits for event)
must return all queued buffers to userspace (V4L2_BUF_FLAG_DONE) and cancel device-side work

codecControls.note: dedicated wire path with v4l2_ext_control pointer fixups (see driver scatterlist_builder ext_ctrls functions)

drainAndFlush.must: V4L2_DEC_CMD_STOP drains (send after queuing all packets; device completes after emitting all decoded frames then V4L2_EVENT_EOS), V4L2_DEC_CMD_START resumes

events.must: support at least V4L2_EVENT_EOS, V4L2_EVENT_SOURCE_CHANGE; decoder resolution change uses SOURCE_CHANGE

events.note: guest driver serves queued events; device side emits VIRTIO_MEDIA_EVT_EVENT

highlights.m2mBufTypes: single-planar M2M: stock userspace uses V4L2_BUF_TYPE_VIDEO_CAPTURE(1) and VIDEO_OUTPUT(2). The compiled host device rejects _MPLANE(9/10) and is exposed as V4L2_CAP_VIDEO_M2M.

errorAndEventSequencing.ioctlErrors: resp.hdr.status carries the full negative Linux errno (e.g. -EINVAL=-22, -EAGAIN=-11). The guest driver propagates it to userspace.
errorAndEventSequencing.sessionCorruption: On fatal device-side session failure send VIRTIO_MEDIA_EVT_ERROR once, then stop using the session id; the guest driver closes it.
errorAndEventSequencing.dqbufFlow: 1) userspace QBUF -> driver forwards metadata, device copies/validates and holds the buffer as queued; 2) device completes buffer -> VIRTIO_MEDIA_EVT_DQBUF; 3) driver completes userspace DQBUF (or already-blocked DQBUF ioctl). Ordering per queue per session is FIFO unless the buffer pipeline reorders (decoder reordering must be hidden inside the device; returned buffers still carry correct sequence/timestamps).
errorAndEventSequencing.eosFlow: Decoder drain: device receives DEC_CMD_STOP, finishes all output, sends remaining DQBUF events, then V4L2_EVENT_EOS (type V4L2_EVENT_EOS). Encoder flush likewise.
errorAndEventSequencing.streamoff: STREAMOFF must synchronously complete/cancel all queued buffers for that queue and report them DONE via the normal DQBUF path before the ioctl response (or in a bounded window right after), matching V4L2 semantics that STREAMOFF returns all owned buffers.

provenance.distinction: Everything above marked with a struct name/number is ACTUAL upstream vendored driver behavior (verified against vendored source). The 'recommended' config values and 'must' implementation notes are PROPOSALS for the primary's VideoToolbox device, clearly separated here.
